findings.condition: productKey() computes the SINGLE-product commercial key via `const f=m.items[0]!.family` -- it blindly reads the first array element of HoldMember.items instead of filtering to the non-wear (gear) item. Prior to this PR, `items` for a SINGLE member could only ever contain equipment families, so index [0] was safe. This PR adds WEAR_JACKET/WEAR_PANTS as valid item families that may coexist in the *same* member's items array (via `m.wear===true`), and parseConditions() in hold.ts (line ~29-33) validates this SINGLE+wear combination as fully well-formed with no constraint on item ordering (schema has no array-ordering rule; `new Set(m.items.map(i=>i.family)).size!==m.items.length` only forbids duplicate families, not ordering).
findings.impact: A staff member with HOLD_EDIT+QUOTE_CREATE (reachable directly via the existing /api/holds and /api/quotes HTTP routes, bypassing the RecommendationWorkspace UI which never emits SINGLE+wear conditions) can submit a member such as {product:'SINGLE',wear:true,tier:'REGULAR',age:'ADULT',items:[{family:'WEAR_JACKET',...},{family:'WEAR_PANTS',...},{family:'POLE',...}]}. Because WEAR_JACKET/WEAR_PANTS is first, `f` resolves to 'WEAR_JACKET', so `kind` falls into the `f==='POLE'?'POLES_ONLY':'BOOTS_ONLY'` else-branch, producing key `SKI_BOOTS_ONLY_ADULT_STANDARD` instead of the correct `SKI_POLES_ONLY_ADULT_STANDARD`. Both are pre-existing, populated keys in the price table (the productKey() kind enum already names EQUIPMENT_ONLY/POLES_ONLY/BOOTS_ONLY as real single-item product lines), so this does not throw PRODUCT_NOT_OFFERED -- it silently prices the reservation using the wrong single-item product's rate, an immutable-but-wrong quote/price snapshot.
findings.evidence: packages/contracts/src/pricing.ts:23 `const f=m.items[0]!.family;`; packages/contracts/src/hold.ts (parseConditions member loop) permits `m.product==='SINGLE'` with `gear.length===1` computed from `gear=m.items.filter(i=>!isWear(i.family))`, independent of array position, while `needsWear` / wearItems checks only require the two wear families to be present somewhere in `m.items`, not their position; packages/core/src/pricing/quote-service.ts and packages/contracts/src/pricing.ts calculate() (line 28-30) call `productKey(m)` on the raw `input.conditions.members` with no reordering step between HTTP body parsing and this call. No existing test (tests/unit/wear-contract.test.ts, tests/wear/*.ts) exercises product:'SINGLE' combined with wear:true; only SKI_SET/SNOWBOARD_SET+wear paths are covered, and those never reach the buggy branch since `m.product!=='SINGLE'` short-circuits to `${m.product}_${m.age}_${m.tier}` before touching `m.items[0]`.
findings.fix: In productKey(), select the gear item explicitly rather than indexing position 0, e.g. `const gearItem=m.items.find(i=>!isWear(i.family));if(!gearItem)throw new PricingError('PRODUCT_NOT_OFFERED');const f=gearItem.family;` (isWear is already exported from ./hold). Alternatively/also, reject SINGLE+wear combinations at parseConditions() until the pricing/allocation layers are audited for every place that assumes `items[0]` is the equipment item.
findings.test: Add a case to tests/unit/wear-contract.test.ts constructing a HoldConditions member with product:'SINGLE', wear:true, tier:'REGULAR', and items ordered as [WEAR_JACKET, WEAR_PANTS, POLE] (wear items listed before the gear item); assert productKey(member) (or calculate()'s resulting line item productKey) equals the POLES_ONLY key, not BOOTS_ONLY, and assert the computed unitJpy/lineJpy matches the pole-single price rather than the boots-single price. Add the mirrored case with gear listed first to confirm both orderings price identically.

The full E10-E13 milestone, serialized equipment loan/return writes, continuous scan return UI, real custody reintegration, Square Sandbox/webhook transport, and physical-phone verification remain explicitly blocked/not implemented, independent of this verdict on the submitted, implemented code.
